the extent of protein chlorination, nitrosylation, and oxidation is elevated in type 2 diabetic patients.

the development of a sensitive and reliable assay for the quantification of the extents of chlorinating, nitration, oxidation, and nitrosylation of hemoglobin in diabetic patients.

the development of a sensitive mass spectrometry assay for the simultaneous quantification of protein modification by reactive chlorine, nitrogen and oxygen species and the application of this method for the study of the effect of diabetes on the extents of these modifications in hemoglobin.
the development of a method for quantifying protein modification by reactive chlorine, nitrogen and oxygen species in human blood.

the extent of chlorinated hemoglobin at α-Tyr is higher in type 2 diabetic subjects and that the extent of methionine oxidation is higher with age in all subjects and nonsmokers.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the extent of modification on hemoglobin is significantly different between diabetic patients and healthy controls, and the extent of modification is correlated to the HbA1C level and the BMI of patients.

the extent of protein chlorination at αTyr-24 in hemoglobin is higher in diabetic patients than in healthy individuals, suggesting the potential of using this modification to evaluate the extent of protein damage.
the extent of chlorinated, nitrated, and oxidized hemoglobin is significantly higher in type 2 diabetes patients, suggesting that these PTMs may be used as biomarkers of diabetes.
